# of professional teams that used sync in the last month

The one number that prices the company. $1B = ARR × multiple, and teams drive both: revenue now (every team pays), revenue later (titles end, teams renew and stay embedded), and the multiple itself (every professional team on sync is a team competitors don't have). The only metric every function can act on: marketing makes teams arrive, product keeps them, research makes more kinds of teams possible. Revenue can't be acted on directly; teams can. Mission: proliferate our tools to every professional team.
↳ reported by: net, gross adds, gross losses split by door.
Show the moving parts: new teams in, teams lost, and the net.
How much money we actually made. We read this number; teams manage the inputs that move it.
Where the money comes from. Product revenue (usage + subs) is worth more per dollar than services revenue when someone values the company.
Last month × 12, a quick way to talk about our size. Never a target on its own.
Of every dollar we make, how much we keep after compute and delivery costs. Revenue can grow while this quietly gets worse, so we watch it.
Product margin should improve as we scale. Services margin buys studio relationships. The split shows which business we're becoming.
How much cash we spend per month, and how many months the money lasts. The $5M has to reach the finish line. Next version: burn multiple (matt is building the dashboard).

Why this is a guardrail: we could grow active teams by dropping prices, and quietly shrink the business. NDR stops that trade. Of what existing customers paid us last year, how much are they paying now? Above 100% means customers grow on their own. We're at 57.6%. The job is driving revenue WHILE growing teams, never one by sacrificing the other. TRIP: below 100%.
↳ split by door: VD / ADR / prosumer / enterprise / preferred / channel
Same doors as the north star. The overall number says how bad; the split says where.
How much of our money comes from one payer. If they leave, how much leaves with them? TRIP: biggest payer over 25% of total.
↳ top-1 and top-3 counterparty, % of total
top-1 catches "one phone call can kill us"; top-3 catches three accounts quietly becoming half the business

Of the teams currently giving us money (subscription, contract, or credit balance), how many actually used us this month? Catches teams that pay but went quiet; those churn next. Pay-as-you-go teams aren't counted: when they stop using, they stop paying, and that shows up elsewhere. TRIP: falling two months in a row.
